questions: Do the iteration 6 metrics match iteration 0 (score 26.0449) exactly? If so, geometry and controller gain changes have both failed to move the outcome, and the next step should be a data pipeline check.
With kp 3.0 on this frozen geometry, does line_loss_events fall below one, or does max_error fall below 0.06 m on any track?
Does steering_oscillation rise sharply with kp 3.0 on the slalom? If so, the controller needs damping (kd) rather than more geometry.
Please report per-step telemetry for one trial per track, showing the step and progress at which the first line loss begins, and whether it occurs at the course start or at a specific bend.

intent: Freeze geometry at the current best-supported platform (y = 0.07 m, 16 mm footprint, ±0.03 m spread, wheel_radius 0.03 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, body 0.12 × 0.18 m, mass 0.8 kg). Geometry is unchanged from iteration 5, so the Integrator's controller gain test (kp 3.0) is the only variable this iteration. I expect line_loss_events and max_error to move only if steering response is the limit.
learning: Five geometry changes (spread, footprint, wheel track, wheel radius, lead) have moved max_error only within 0.060 to 0.061 m, and iteration 5 reproduced the iteration-0 baseline exactly. Geometry is probably no longer the binding limit. If the controller gain test fails to clear the line, the remaining untested geometry levers are mass (0.4 to 1.5 kg) and body_length, which I would test next on a fixed controller. Neither can lift the 0.06 m off-track floor directly, so they are low expected value.
rationale: Iteration 5 (sensor row moved to y = 0.07 m, 16 mm footprint, ±0.03 m spread, wheel_radius 0.03 m, wheel_track 0.12 m) scored 26.0449. That is identical to the iteration-0 baseline on all three tracks (max_error 0.0614, 0.0611, 0.0609; one line-loss event per trial; progress 0.115, 0.04, 0.035; no finishes). The forward lead therefore has no measurable effect. Across five geometry families (spread, footprint, wheel track, wheel radius, lead), max_error has stayed at 0.060 to 0.061 m and every run ends off track after one line-loss event. Only iteration 4 (wheel_radius 0.04 m) moved the metrics, and it scored lower. The off-track floor of 0.06 m binds, and body_width cannot lift it: even 0.18 m gives 0.0575 m. The Integrator's rule (a) applies: when the metrics match the baseline, geometry is exhausted for the current controller. I therefore freeze the geometry at its current best-supported values so the Integrator can test controller gain (kp 3.0) on a fixed platform. I keep y = 0.07 m, the last tested lead, which is metrically equivalent to the baseline. Changing mass or body length now would confound the gain test, and neither can lift the 0.06 m floor directly. Expected result: geometry is unchanged, so any change in outcome comes from the controller. I expect the kp change to be the first lever that moves line_loss_events or max_error. If the metrics again match iteration 0 exactly, the Integrator should treat the controller, not geometry, as the blocker.
